title: Scaloni finalises Argentina XI for friendly against Iceland
text:
The Argentina National Team will hold its final training session this afternoon before Tuesday’s friendly against Iceland, starting at 10 p.m. at Jordan-Hare Stadium in Alabama, as part of its preparation for the 2026 World Cup, and coach Lionel Scaloni will decide on the starting eleven after the press conference he gives ahead of training.

The Albiceleste squad will begin working at 8:30 p.m. (Argentina time) at the stadium, and the first 15 minutes will be open to the press, so they can be followed live on TyC Sports. The coach will use this session to finalize the lineup, some names of which are already beginning to emerge.

The biggest expectation ahead of the match against the Nordic side will be what role Scaloni gives Lionel Messi, who, now recovered from the discomfort he arrived with from Inter Miami, did not play any minutes against Honduras. The idea is for him to gain match fitness in this friendly, but it has not yet been decided whether he will start or come on in the second half.

On the other hand, everything indicates that after Juan Musso got his chance against the Central Americans on Saturday, this time Gerónimo Rulli will start. The former Estudiantes de La Plata player is the coaching staff’s first alternative in goal in case Emiliano Martínez cannot play. Dibu is recovering from a fracture to the ring finger on his right hand, but he should have no trouble being ready for the debut against Algeria on Tuesday the 16th.

Argentina National Team training in Kansas.

At the same time, it remains to be seen what Scaloni decides regarding the rest of the team. Lisandro Martínez and Cristian Romero could be the center-back pairing. Cuti has already recovered from the ligament injury he suffered at Tottenham, got minutes against Honduras, and could feature again to keep getting up to speed. Meanwhile, Nicolás Tagliafico finished fatigued, so Facundo Medina could be the left back.

At right back, it remains to be seen whether the coach finally gives Nicolás Capaldo a chance, since Agustín Giay played the first friendly. Both defenders were called up due to the injuries to Nahuel Molina and Gonzalo Montiel and, if they are not fully fit for the World Cup, they could compete for a place on the roster. The truth is that both trained alongside the group yesterday for the first time, as did Nicolás Paz, and they have been making progress, but the coach has already said he will make the decision after the friendly.

Likewise, in midfield, Rodrigo De Paul, Enzo Fernández, and Alexis Mac Allister have a better chance of starting, after not being in the lineup from the beginning on Saturday. It remains to be seen whether Exequiel Palacios gets another chance or whether that fourth midfield spot goes to Thiago Almada, who had a good match against Honduras. Another option is for Nicolás González to get his chance, another player who had arrived in the United States injured but is now available. Up front, he could stick with Lautaro Martínez or give more minutes to José Manuel López, who came on in the last match.

For now, the only injured players are Dibu, Leandro Paredes, and Julián Álvarez. The case drawing the most attention — and concern — is that of the Boca midfielder. Paredes is still rehabbing the hamstring muscle injury he suffered in the Copa Libertadores match against Universidad Católica and continues to train separately. As for the forward, he is dealing with inflammation in his left ankle as a result of the sprain he suffered during the Champions League semifinals with Atlético de Madrid. It is worth mentioning that Leonardo Balerdi has already been ruled out due to a soleus injury, and his replacement on the 26-man roster has not yet been decided.

Gerónimo Rulli; Nicolás Capaldo or Agustín Giay, Cristian Romero, Lisandro Martínez, Facundo Medina; Rodrigo De Paul, Enzo Fernández, Alexis Mac Allister, Exequiel Palacios; Lionel Messi and Lautaro Martínez or José Manuel López
